title: Developer experience docs: SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, and canonical fixes
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Overview

This document defines the standard templates, operating procedures, and canonical fixes for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation focused on: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues with canonical resolutions. The goal is to keep end-user-facing docs consistent, discoverable, and operationally reliable for engineers and customers integrating Redwood Inference.

Goals

- Provide a single source of truth for DevEx documentation structure and publishing workflow.
- Reduce first-touch support time by surfacing canonical fixes in docs.
- Ensure SDK and API examples are runnable, tested, and versioned.
- Maintain a lightweight review and deprecation policy with clear ownership.

Audience

- SDK authors and maintainers
- Developer advocates and technical writers
- Solutions engineers and support on-call
- Product engineers shipping API changes

Ownership and Roles

- Document owner: DevEx docs owner (engineering). Responsible for edits, publishing, and triage.
- Reviewers: SDK leads and Solutions Engineering for correctness.
- Approver: DevEx manager for policy changes.
- Support liaison: Customer Success engineer assigned to surface top issues.

Folder and File Naming Standards

- Folder: eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/ for quickstarts and SDK templates.
- Filenames: short-descriptive, dash-separated, include year when applicable, .json for the source export. Example: sdk-quickstart-node-2026.json
- Document title in metadata must match top-level H1/intro title.

Docs Template (required fields)

Every user-facing doc must include the following fields at top-level (Confluence content + metadata):

1) Short intro (1-3 sentences)
2) Prerequisites / requirements (OS, SDK versions, API keys)
3) Step-by-step quickstart (1-6 steps)
4) Complete runnable example (copy-pasteable)
5) Troubleshooting / "If you see this" table
6) Links to related pages and SDK reference

Example metadata table (copy into the Confluence metadata macro):

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| title | <short descriptive title> |
| space | eng-developer-experience |
| author | <full name> |
| owner_team | engineering |
| status | draft |
| created_at | YYYY-MM-DD |
| last_updated | YYYY-MM-DD |

SDK Guide: Structure and Minimal Example

Structure recommendations:
- Overview and when to use the SDK vs raw API.
- Installation (pip/npm/go get).
- Authentication examples for hosted, dedicated, and private endpoints.
- Core usage patterns (text generation, chat, embeddings, streaming).
- Error handling and retry guidance (status codes, idempotency).
- Rate limit expectations and backoff policy.
- Link to API reference and changelog.

Minimal Python SDK example (runnable snippet):

```python
# Prereqs: python 3.9+, pip install redwood-sdk>=0.8.0
from redwood_sdk import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1-small", prompt="Write a short haiku about latency.")
print(resp.text)
```

Guidelines for code examples:
- Use environment variables for credentials.
- Keep examples minimal: show success path and one common failure handling case.
- Pin to a minor SDK version in examples and add a note when the example was last validated.

Quickstarts and Templates (Node, Python, Curl)

We provide three canonical quickstarts that must be kept up to date. Each quickstart must have: Title, TL;DR, Prereqs, Step list, Full example, and Validation step.

Node (example)
1. Prereqs: Node 18+, npm install @redwood/inference-js
2. Steps:
   a. Set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env
   b. npm run quickstart (script provided)
3. Validation: curl the local script endpoint or check console output contains "generated_text"

Curl (minimal generation)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","prompt":"Hello from Redwood"}'

API Examples: canonical patterns

- Text generation: single-shot prompt + top_p/top_k guidance.
- Streaming: show client-side loop and how to handle reconnects.
- Embeddings: example showing vector normalization and similarity query.
- Function/tool calling: example request + sample JSON schema and how to handle tool invocation.

Streaming example note:
- Include a small resilient client pseudocode that reconnects on 5xx or socket timeout with exponential backoff (jitter).
- Recommend 60s idle timeout handling and a 10s read deadline in examples.

Docs Site Operating Procedures

Publishing checklist (must be completed before setting status = published):
- [ ] Content validated for factual accuracy by an SDK owner.
- [ ] Code examples executed against staging and verified.
- [ ] Spell-check and style pass (DevEx style guide).
- [ ] Links and related_pages updated.
- [ ] Add labels and reviewers in metadata.
- [ ] SLO for doc responsiveness set (see below).

Review cadence and SLOs:
- Minor docs updates: 3 business day review target.
- Major changes (API surface changes): 5 business day review target + cross-team review.
- Doc responsiveness SLO: 90% of published bug-fix changes merged within 7 calendar days after issue reported. Owner must triage within 24 hours.

Testing and CI for docs examples

- All runnable examples are stored in the devex-examples repo and are executed in a nightly matrix (python/node/curl).
- Failures open a "docs-examples" issue on GitHub and notify #devex on Slack.
- Maintain a tests/validation.md in each example folder describing the validation command.

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (current top 10)

1) Symptom: "401 / invalid API key"
   - Root cause: Missing/expired key or wrong environment used (private deployments require different endpoint).
   - Canonical fix: Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY and ensure endpoint matches deployment (hosted vs private). Add example export command.
   - Doc link: quickstart auth section.

2) Symptom: "Rate limit 429 on burst load"
   - Root cause: No batching or quota exceeded for the API key.
   - Canonical fix: Implement client-side batching or request quota increase; include exponential backoff with caps.
   - Doc link: SDK error handling and quotas.

3) Symptom: "Streaming client disconnects intermittently"
   - Root cause: Socket idle timeout, proxy limits, or long-running inference without keepalive.
   - Canonical fix: Use incremental keepalive pings, reduce model max_tokens, and add reconnect logic.
   - Doc link: streaming guide.

4) Symptom: "Embeddings mismatch / poor search results"
   - Root cause: Missing vector normalization, inconsistent embedding model versions.
   - Canonical fix: Normalize vectors, add model version to index metadata, re-index when migrating models.
   - Doc link: embeddings best practices.

5) Symptom: "High latency on short prompts"
   - Root cause: Incorrect model selection or cold-cache on dedicated/private pools.
   - Canonical fix: Recommend low-latency model variants and enable prefix caching; add guidance on warm-up requests during deployment.
   - Doc link: latency tuning guide.

6) Symptom: "Inconsistent chat state / token overlap"
   - Root cause: Incorrect conversation state serialization or duplicate system messages.
   - Canonical fix: Use provided ChatSession helper from SDK which manages tokens and deduplication.
   - Doc link: chat API examples.

7) Symptom: "Unexpected model fallback behavior"
   - Root cause: Routing policy triggers fallback to cheaper model variant without full compatibility checks.
   - Canonical fix: Pin required model version in request metadata or update rollout policy.
   - Doc link: routing and fallbacks.

8) Symptom: "Large token bill after short test"
   - Root cause: Using high max_tokens with logprobs/debug mode or failing to chunk long inputs.
   - Canonical fix: Set conservative max_tokens during dev and enable truncation/chunking examples.
   - Doc link: cost-control best practices.

9) Symptom: "Function calling returns invalid JSON"
   - Root cause: Model returned free-form text or schema mismatch.
   - Canonical fix: Use explicit JSON schema in function call options and post-validate responses against schema.
   - Doc link: function calling guide.

10) Symptom: "Private deployment auth errors"
    - Root cause: KMS/HSM misconfiguration or missing root CA in on-prem env.
    - Canonical fix: Verify KMS access, rotate keys per guide, and import CA certs to client trust store.
    - Doc link: private deployment onboarding.

For each canonical fix, include a minimal repro snippet in the linked quickstart and a ticket template to open if fix does not resolve the issue.

Ticket template for unresolved issues:
1. Title: [Docs-CanonicalFix] <short description>
2. Steps to reproduce: minimal reproducible steps and environment (SDK version, deployment type)
3. Expected vs actual behavior
4. Logs / error messages / request ids
5. Reproduction repo or gist attached
6. Owner assigned and initial triage notes

Deprecation and Rollout policy for examples

- When an API or SDK behavior changes, the old example should be deprecated for 30 days with both old and new examples visible and clearly labeled.
- After 30 days, move old example to an archive folder and update links.
- Major breaking changes require a 60-day deprecation window and a public changelog entry.

Monitoring and Metrics for docs health

- Example CI pass rate (nightly): target >= 98%.
- Support triage time: median <= 24 hours.
- Top-issue re-open rate: target < 5% after canonical fix published.

References and related pages

- Developer Experience docs site operating procedures (internal)
- SDK reference pages for python/node/go
- DevEx examples repo: github.com/redwood-inference/devex-examples

How to update this document

1. Fork the page in Confluence and add your changes to a draft.
2. Add reviewers for the affected SDK/area.
3. Run the example validation scripts and attach logs.
4. Once approved, change status to published and add release note to the DevEx changelog.

Contact and escalation

- Primary owner: DevEx docs (devex@redwood.ai)
- Support channel: #devex on Slack for triage
- Escalation: assign to on-call Docs engineer and notify Solutions Engineering for customer-impacting issues.

Appendix: common CLI commands

- Validate Python example: python tests/validate_python_example.py --example=quickstart-hello
- Run Node quickstart locally: NODE_ENV=development REDWOOD_API_KEY=$KEY node quickstart.js
- Re-run docs CI for examples: .github/workflows/docs-examples/re-run.sh

Document change log

- 2026-02-20: Updated streaming guidance and added SLOs for doc responsiveness.
